title: POC scoping - data audit & redaction benchmarks (Helios Health)
summary: Kickoff for a limited POC focused on data handling: redaction, retention, and prompt storage. Agreed success criteria include zero persistent PII in logs, <75ms median token latency for most inferences in hosted mode, and reproducible benchmark spreadsheet. Timeline: 6 week POC with week 1 baseline benchmarks and week 4 integration tests. Next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + redaction whitepaper, Helios to provide sample (anonymized) payloads and traffic profile.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (latency, throughput, token cost)
Data handling: PII, redaction, prompt storage, retention
action_items: Priya: Share SOC 2 attestation, security pack, and redaction whitepaper by 2025-06-16
Ethan: Draft benchmark runbook and metric dashboard template by 2025-06-18
Jared: Provide 48-hour sample traffic profile and 10 representative prompts (anonymized) by 2025-06-15
Maya: Confirm internal review stakeholders for privacy signoff by 2025-06-20
Carlos: Schedule access window for Helios test VPC (if needed) in week 3
next_steps: Redwood to send security artifacts + SSO/KMS integration notes
Helios to prepare sanitized sample dataset and traffic patterns
Schedule benchmark kickoff (1 hour) in week 1 once artifacts received
Agree on canary traffic shaping for retention/redaction verification
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Shah (AE): All right, thanks everyone for joining. Uh, this is Priya from Redwood, Ethan's here as well, hi Ethan. Today we want to scope the POC around your data handling concerns—especially redaction and retention—and nail down success criteria and benchmarks. Carlos, Maya, do you want to kick off with your primary goals?

[00:18] Carlos Vega (CTO): Yeah, sure. Hi, everyone. For Helios, the big thing is patient PII. We can't have any persistent logs that could leak identifiers. We're also worried about prompt storage—our legal team wants assurances about retention windows, and we need to replicate some real-world traffic to validate latency and cost.

[00:36] Maya Lin (Head of Data Privacy): And to add, we need an auditable trail showing redaction took place, and ideally automated proofs that, you know, certain fields were stripped. We have to sign off from compliance before any production.

[00:49] Ethan Moore (SE): Totally get that. We usually approach this with a 3-part plan: 1) baseline benchmark with synthetic or sanitized payloads, 2) redaction verification runs where we inject PII tokens and assert they do not persist in logs, and 3) integration test in a private VPC or Dedicated environment if you need it.

[01:07] Aisha Khan (Product): Quick question — for the POC do we need Redwood Private or can we use hosted? Cost-wise hosted is easier but privacy team prefers VPC.

[01:15] Priya Shah: For scoping, let's keep both options open. We can run initial benchmarks on hosted to validate latency and token costs, and if you need network isolation or KMS-backed keys we can pivot to Dedicated or Private in week 3. That will affect timelines.

[01:29] Jared Frost (ML Engineer): What kind of latency numbers should we expect? Our downstream app needs sub-100ms med per-token when doing short prompts — is that realistic?

[01:37] Ethan Moore: Short prompts with modern quantized models on our hosted clusters usually hit med per-token latency in the 30–80ms range depending on sequence length and batching. For production-like loads we recommend continuous batching offload; we'll put exact expectations in the benchmark runbook. There might be noise on the first few tokens due to KV cache warming.

[01:55] Carlos: Okay. Success criteria — we're thinking: 1) no PII in logs within 48 hours of deletion request, 2) latency within agreed SLO for 95th pctl, 3) runbook shows reproducible results. Does that align?

[02:08] Priya: Yes, that aligns. Might want to be explicit: deletion request triggers a retention policy to purge prompt storage and any cached KV entries tied to that session — we'll document the exact flows.

[02:20] Maya: Also need to know where prompt history is stored. Is it in Redwood logs by default? Is it encrypted at rest? Are prompts used for model training?

[02:30] Ethan: Default is ephemeral logs for diagnostics; for hosted we persist limited metadata and allow prompt storage settings to be toggled. Everything at rest is encrypted with service-managed keys unless you bring your own KMS in Private/Dedicated. And no, we do not use customer prompts to train models — we'll include that in the security pack as well.

[02:48] Maya: Good, please put that in writing.

[02:52] Priya: Absolutely. We'll attach explicit statements: retention windows, encryption, training policy.

[03:00] Jared: On redaction—do you offer on-the-fly redaction or post-hoc redaction jobs? We want a two-step: pre-send client-side redaction patterns + server-side verification.

[03:10] Ethan: Common approach is client-side tokenization/redaction for obvious PII (SSNs, MRNs) and then server-side policy enforcement. For the POC we can run an automated verification harness that injects sentinel PII values to ensure they do not appear in persisted logs. We also support configurable redaction rules.

[03:29] Maya: Sentinel tests sound good. We need audit trail proving they ran.

[03:33] Priya: We'll produce a runbook that logs test IDs and timestamps. Those entries are, of course, themselves handled under the same retention policy.

[03:41] Carlos: Let's talk traffic. Jared, what's our expected qps and token distribution?

[03:46] Jared Frost: For the initial feature, expect about 30 rps peak with most requests under 200 tokens. We'll provide a 48-hour sample trace. There is a tail of longer summaries up to 1,200 tokens but that's <5% of traffic.

[03:58] Ethan: That helps. For CPU/GPU sizing we'll model the 95th percentile, and the benchmark will include throughput curves at 10, 20, 30 rps and the long-tail 1k-token requests.

[04:10] Aisha: Costs matter too. Can you estimate token cost differential if we enable persistent prompt storage vs ephemeral?

[04:16] Priya: We'll add a cost sensitivity sheet. Typically storage affects cost mainly via retrieval and debugging tokens; persistent indexing and search add fixed overhead. We'll run both modes in the POC to show delta.

[04:28] Maya: On deletion timeframe, we need proof that data is removed within our legal SLA — which is 72 hours for certain categories. Can Redwood support programmatic deletion hooks?

[04:38] Ethan: Yes. We have APIs to trigger retention purges and a policy engine to set TTLs at route level. For Private deployments you can have immediate purge via KMS key rotation paradigms. We'll show examples.

[04:51] Carlos: We might need to see a dry-run where you delete a few entries and we confirm by running queries against logs.

[04:56] Priya: Agreed. Week 2 we'll run deletion validation tests and provide artifacts.

[05:00] Maya: About prompt storage: we want ability to disable prompt retention for certain routes (e.g., any route with PHI). Can that be per-route?

[05:08] Ethan: Yes, per-route retention policy is supported. You can also mask or tokenize before storage. We'll include config examples in the runbook.

[05:16] Jared: Benchmarks — what metrics exactly will you gather? Latency, throughput, token counts, KV cache hit rate?

[05:22] Ethan: We'll capture median and p95 latency per token, end-to-end request latency, tokens generated, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit/miss rates, and cost estimates. We'll surface them in a simple dashboard and share raw CSVs.

[05:36] Carlos: We need reproducibility. If you run the benchmark again next week we should see comparable numbers within a tolerance.

[05:43] Ethan: We'll pin model versions and quantization settings, and record environment metadata—everything to reproduce.

[05:50] Aisha: Timeline? You mentioned six weeks earlier — can you outline milestone weeks?

[05:55] Priya: Proposed: Week 0 (this week) finalize scope and artifacts; Week 1 baseline benchmarks with sanitized payloads; Week 2 redaction and deletion validation; Week 3 optional Private/Dedicated switch and integration tests; Week 4 run production-like traffic; Week 5 wrap up and SOW / summary report. That's roughly 5–6 calendar weeks.

[06:18] Carlos: That works as a starter. We're constrained by our compliance review too, might add a week.

[06:24] Maya: For CISO signoff we need SOC2, ISO docs, vulnerability scan results and a short data flow diagram.

[06:31] Priya: We'll attach SOC2 Type II, sample dataflow diagram, and recent vuln scan summary.

[06:36] Jared: One concern — if we use hosted and later move to Dedicated, will results be comparable? Kernel selection, quantization can change latency.

[06:44] Ethan: Good point. We'll make a mapping table of runtime differences and expected performance delta. When migrating to Dedicated we recommend a quick re-run of the core benchmarks; we'll keep models consistent.

[06:55] Maya: Also, any chance of accidental retention via logs from debugging endpoints?

[07:01] Priya: We'll disable debug-level logs in POC runs unless explicitly enabled. Debug logs are gated and marked for shorter retention.

[07:08] Carlos: Ok. Let's cover acceptance tests: 1) sentinel PII injection shows zero persisted matches after purge; 2) latency within agreed SLO at 95th; 3) cost per 1k tokens below agreed threshold; 4) security artifacts provided.

[07:25] Priya: I'll formalize those into the acceptance criteria doc and circulate.

[07:30] Aisha: On the benchmark harness — will you share the scripts? We want to run them in our environment to validate.

[07:36] Ethan: Yes, we'll provide the harness and Dockerized runners so you can run locally or in your VPC.

[07:42] Maya: For redaction rules, can we supply custom regexes? We have some proprietary identifiers that aren't standard formats.

[07:48] Ethan: Absolutely. The policy engine supports custom regex and ML-based detectors. We'll include examples for attaching custom rules to routes.

[07:58] Carlos: Anything about legal or procurement? We may need a data processing addendum.

[08:02] Priya: Finance and legal will follow up; procurement usually wants a DPA + SOW if we move to Dedicated. We'll make sure templates are included.

[08:10] Maya: One more — can we get a sample of the logs (sanitized) so our auditors can see format?

[08:15] Priya: Yes, we'll include sample sanitized logs and a mapping of log fields.

[08:20] (short cross-talk)

[08:24] Ethan: Quick note on KV cache: we can tie cache TTLs to session IDs and purge on deletion events, but if a model's internal KV has already been used in an in-flight session we need to flush or invalidate. We'll show approaches.

[08:36] Jared: Good — we need that for clinical summarization flows because old patient context leaking would be bad.

[08:42] Priya: Totally. We'll demo a cache invalidation run.

[08:47] Carlos: Let's lock next meeting: benchmark kickoff when Redwood sends artifacts. How about Monday 2025-06-16 at 10am PT?

[08:56] Maya: Works for me.

[08:57] Priya: Works for us too. We'll send calendar invite and the artifacts before then.

[09:03] Priya (wrap): Recap — Redwood sends SOC2, redaction whitepaper, benchmark runbook; Helios sends sanitized traffic and prompts; schedule kickoff for 6/16. Action owners captured. Thanks, everyone.

[09:15] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts; speaker labels are best-effort.
